claims.text: A combinatorial high-throughput composition-spread synthesis approach can systematically vary the percentages of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr in an alloy library.
Changing individual elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr will produce non-linear changes in mechanical properties.
Some HfNbTaTiZr compositional regions will have greater hardness than the equiatomic baseline.
Some HfNbTaTiZr compositional regions will have greater tensile strength than the equiatomic baseline.
Other compositional regions may have mechanical properties below those of the equiatomic baseline.
Optimized lattice distortion can enhance strengthening in HfNbTaTiZr.
Grain-size or grain-boundary effects can alter the hardness of HfNbTaTiZr.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is equiatomic or near-equiatomic.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy forms a single-phase solid solution under standard synthesis conditions.
Elemental-ratio changes cause local variations in lattice distortion.
Elemental-ratio changes alter interatomic bonding.
Changes in lattice distortion and interatomic bonding modulate dislocation mobility.
Modulation of dislocation mobility changes solid-solution strengthening.
Composition-induced grain-size changes can modify grain-boundary strengthening.
Spark plasma sintering of low-oxygen gas-atomized HfNbTaTiZr powder can produce a promising specimen suitable for subsequent microstructural refinement.
High-pressure torsion can refine the HfNbTaTiZr microstructure to a grain size below 5 in the unit reported by the truncated evidence record.
High-pressure-torsion-processed HfNbTaTiZr can reach a hardness of 410 HV10.
The proposed response is restricted to compositions that retain a single-phase microstructure.
The proposed mechanical-property response is restricted to room-temperature, quasi-static loading.
Nanoindentation, miniaturized tensile testing, XRD, and electron microscopy can jointly map mechanical properties and local microstructure across the composition spread.
